adapt-sizes.notes: Inspected promo.vixl, then made both sizes and the PNGs in one vixl_adapt_layout call (sizes as {width,height,name} so the {name}-{size} template gave promo-story / promo-banner). Checked both copies and previewed the banner. Friction: (1) vixl_check on both copies fails (passed=false, action 'fix') only because of a fonts warning the source already had (bundled fallback font). The brief says not to change the original, and adapt_layout gives no hint about it, so the copies 'fail' validation while their layout is fine. (2) In the story copy the logo moved from x=960 to x=946 with 'anchor: right, top' and no reason given. It looks like a safe-area nudge, but the layer report doesn't say so. (3) adapt_layout leaves the source and both copies open in the shared server, so it took 3 close calls plus a vixl_workspace_list to see what was open. (4) The export outcomes say 'review required: export runs no checks', which is noise when the agent checks right after.
adapt-sizes.agent_answer: Made promo-story.vixl (1080x1920) and promo-banner.vixl (1200x628) from promo.vixl with title, button and logo on canvas, and exported promo-story.png and promo-banner.png; the original is unchanged.

errors: operations_apply: page action 'set' on page 1 of a new document failed with 'This document has no pages yet; create one with page add'. A fresh document has no page 1, so the first slide must also be made with page add.
deck-pptx.notes: Created a 1280x720 slides document with a navy background, then added three pages with page add (background, name, select) and a centered white 96px heading on each. The notes 'Thank the team' went on page 3. Previewed page='all', checked with pages='all', and exported deck.pptx and deck.pdf in one vixl_export_batch. Friction: (1) I expected the existing canvas to count as page 1. Needing 'add' for the first page surprised me, though the error message said exactly what to do. (2) vixl_check with pages='all' plus deck checks repeats the deck-level findings once per page, so 2 real findings came back as 6. (3) title_position flagged slide 3 because its centered title is narrower and so starts at a different x ('sits at x 410 where the other titles sit at 288'). With centered titles that is a false positive; the check compares left edges, not alignment. (4) The 'notes' warning that pages 1-2 have no notes is fair but noisy when the brief asks for notes on one slide only. (5) The PPTX export warns that Roboto is not embedded. That is useful, and the PDF embeds it.
deck-pptx.agent_answer: Made a three-slide navy deck (Quarterly Review / Revenue up 12% / Next steps, with the speaker note 'Thank the team' on slide 3) and exported deck.pptx and deck.pdf.

fix-layout.notes: vixl_check found 5 errors: footer cut off by the canvas, footer outside the safe area, footer contrast unmeasurable (because it was off canvas), title/subtitle text overlap, and subtitle contrast 1.36:1. There was also a fonts warning with action 'fix'. I installed the source-serif-sans pairing, set it on the three text layers with text-set, set the subtitle color to #555555 and moved it to y=340, and moved the footer to (760,1220). The check then came back clean. Friction: (1) vixl_font_pair says 'Layouts now use these fonts by default', but existing text layers keep the fallback font, so each one needed a text-set font. A 'restyle existing text' option would help. (2) The footer contrast error ('Region must be within canvas') is a knock-on of the bounds error, not a separate problem, but it is counted as its own error with no repair. (3) Two different repairs are suggested for the same footer (the bounds nudge and the safe-area nudge), and only the safe-area one fixes both. (4) The text-text overlap has no mechanical repair, though 'move below the other text' would be easy to suggest.
fix-layout.agent_answer: Fixed all of poster.vixl's check errors (overlap, contrast, cut-off footer, safe area) and replaced the fallback font, without deleting or rewording text; vixl_check is now clean.

form-registration.notes: Created a letter page (2550x3300 at 300 dpi) with a white background. One batch did all of it: form options (title, lang, reading tab order), a heading, visible text labels, and the fields. full_name and email are required text fields linked with label_layer, and email has format email. The two plan radios share key 'plan' with options annual and monthly. There is a newsletter checkbox and a signature field. The form, bounds, overlap, contrast, fonts, legibility and accessibility checks passed, including sample='worst'. The show_fields preview confirmed tab order 1-5. Exported registration.pdf with fillable=true. Friction: (1) The fillable PDF export result doesn't report how many fields were written or their keys, so I couldn't confirm the AcroForm from the result. (2) Letter at 300 dpi means sizes in the thousands of pixels; it's easy to choose a label size that's too small without knowing the min-font rule in points. (3) The show_fields overlay tags are drawn over the visible labels, which makes the label/field relationship harder to judge in that view.
form-registration.agent_answer: Built registration.vixl (US letter, white) with a heading and labelled fields full_name*, email* (email format), a plan radio group (annual/monthly), a newsletter checkbox and a signature box. Form checks pass, and I exported registration.pdf as a fillable PDF.

object-detect-cat.notes: Inspected the 7 shapes and worked out the parts from their geometry: s1 tail, s2 body, s3/s4 legs, s5 head, s6/s7 ears. Renamed them, grouped them as 'cat', declared kind cat and named every part (legs and ears with sides). check connected flagged head (7.6 px gap), ear_left and ear_right (157 px away) as floating. I moved the head down 15 px and the ears down 25/85 px so they overlap the head. connected and bounds now pass, and nothing was deleted. Friction: (1) connected reports these as warnings with action 'review', not errors, even though a part 157 px away is plainly broken. (2) The ears' distances are measured to the 'main body', which excluded the floating head, so the numbers (84.7 px) didn't match the ear-to-head gap I had to fix. (3) After the moves, vixl_document_inspect(object='cat') still reported the group bounds as [120,60,280,350], the old top of the right ear at y=60. The ear now starts at y=145, so the group bounds look stale and are not recomputed after children move. (4) Polygon content_bounds (16x18 in a 40x50 box) don't match the drawn triangle's ink, which made the geometry hard to judge without a preview.
object-detect-cat.agent_answer: Grouped pile.vixl's shapes into one cat object with head, body, ears, legs and tail named as parts, and moved the floating head and ears so they connect; no shapes were deleted.

object-person-guitar.notes: Used vixl_guide for the person approach and vixl_resource_get for the guitar parts, and read the pen/shape schemas. Built a flat figure in one batch: legs, feet, torso, upper arms as round-capped pen strokes, the guitar, lower arms, hands, head, hair, eyes and mouth. The guitar is body, sound-hole, bridge, neck, headstock, and strings as a 6-line stroked path. In the second batch I grouped the guitar into 'guitar' (kind guitar, parts named), then grouped everything into 'player' (kind person) and named all 18 person parts with sides. connected and bounds checks are clean. inspect(object='player') shows no missing parts and guitar as a sub-object. Previewed isolate=['player/guitar'] and exported player.png. Friction: (1) person has 10 required part types (eyes, mouth, upper/lower arms and legs, hands and feet, all sided), so naming parts took 28 operations. A bulk 'parts' map on the object op ({layer: part}) or auto-naming from layer names like upper_arm_left would cut this a lot. (2) The guitar proportion rule ('neck length against body height', 0.45-0.7) is ambiguous for a guitar drawn horizontally. (3) In a grouping batch the response repeats every member's coordinates in both group and canvas space, which is very verbose.
object-person-guitar.agent_answer: Made player.vixl (600x700, white) with a person object 'player' playing a guitar sub-object (body, neck, headstock, strings), previewed the guitar alone and exported player.png.

photo-caption.notes: Created a 1080x1350 document and imported photo.jpg (1600x1000). Resized the photo to 1080x675 (aspect kept) at (0,0), added a #1a1a1a caption bar at 0,675 1080x675, and centered white 72px 'Summer Sale – 40% off' text in the bar with within=caption_bar. The check then gave two safe_area review warnings for the full-bleed photo and bar. I marked both as role background with layer-intent, and the check came back clean. Exported post.jpg. Friction: (1) With no background given, document_create rolled a palette background (#fffbe0). I didn't ask for it and it doesn't matter here, but it surprised me. (2) resize needs both width and height. There's no 'width only, keep aspect' path I could see without computing the height myself. (3) Full-bleed images and bars get safe_area warnings by default, so you need to know the layer-intent role trick to make them go away.
photo-caption.agent_answer: Made post.vixl (1080x1350): photo scaled to 1080x675 at the top, a dark caption bar with centered white 72px 'Summer Sale – 40% off', vixl_check clean, exported post.jpg.

roll-applied.notes: Created an 800x800 document, then ran vixl_roll with seed 12, apply=true, locks {layout: hero-statement, pairing: source-serif-sans, palette: ocean} and slots title/subtitle/cta. Fonts came from the cache. vixl_check passed (only info findings) and I previewed the result. Friction: (1) The rolled density 'dense' left the 'hero-statement' headline at 52px on an 800px canvas, timid for a hero layout. (2) It added a 'direction-motif' layer, an 8x2 px accent rectangle at the top right outside the safe area. In the preview it reads as a stray speck, and check silently accepts it as an intentional crop. (3) The fonts from document_create's own roll (public-sans) stay embedded, unused, after the roll swaps the pairing; check reports 112 KB of unused fonts. (4) The roll result is very large: the full baseline guide list (25 guides) is echoed twice.
roll-applied.agent_answer: Created design.vixl at 800x800 and applied the seed-12 roll with layout hero-statement, pairing source-serif-sans and palette ocean, filled with Launch / A new beginning / Learn more; checks pass.

svg-logo-import.notes: Created a 100x100 document, imported logo.svg in editable mode (it became one path shape named 'mark' at 10,10 80x80), moved mark to x=5, checked and previewed, and exported logo.svg.png. Friction: (1) The import's name='logo' parameter seemed to have no effect: the layer kept the SVG id 'mark', which is what the brief needed, but name's meaning is unclear. (2) document_create rolled a dark background (#23252b) for a plain 100x100 canvas with no purpose given, which changes the exported PNG compared with a transparent or white default.
svg-logo-import.agent_answer: Created design.vixl (100x100), imported logo.svg as editable geometry, moved 'mark' to x=5, and exported logo.svg.png.

timeline-motion.notes: Created a 200x100 document with a white background. One batch added the red 20x20 ellipse 'ball' at 0,40, set timeline-set duration 1000 and fps 10, and keyed x at 0 ms (value 0, easing linear) and 1000 ms (value 180). A timeline_preview contact sheet at 0/500/1000 and a single-frame preview at 250 ms confirmed linear motion (ball centre about 55). Exported start.png and end.png with export_batch time=0/1000, and motion.gif (10 frames at 100 ms). Friction: (1) timeline_inspect detail=full doesn't show each key's easing, so I couldn't confirm 'linear' was stored without rendering an in-between frame. (2) export_timeline warns about a loop seam (x ends at 180 but starts at 0) for a one-way move the brief asked for. A non-looping timeline or loop=1 shouldn't warn. (3) The GIF holds frames 0-900 ms, so the 1000 ms end pose (x=180) never appears in it. That is correct for a looping GIF, but worth stating in the result. (4) export_batch per-target results don't echo the time used.
timeline-motion.agent_answer: Made design.vixl (200x100) with a red 20x20 'ball' moving linearly from x=0 to 180 over a 1 s, 10 fps timeline, and exported start.png, end.png and motion.gif.

youtube-thumbnail.notes: Created with size youtube-thumbnail and a dark #111318 background. Added a 130px white heading 'HOW I BUILT IT', a 60px yellow subtitle 'A full app in 48 hours', and a red rounded badge at 1020,56 (190x86) with white 'NEW' centered via within. Checked with safe_area='5%', avoid=[85%,85%,15%,15%], thumbnail_width 320, contrast and color_vision: no issues. Exported thumbnail.png at full size. Friction: the youtube-thumbnail preset's own safe area is 40 px, not 5% (64x36), so the default check doesn't test the brief's rule; I had to pass safe_area and avoid myself. It would help if the preset carried YouTube's timestamp corner as a reserved zone.
youtube-thumbnail.agent_answer: Made thumbnail.vixl (1280x720, dark) with 'HOW I BUILT IT' at 130px, a '48 hours' subtitle and a red NEW badge top-right, inside a 5% safe area and clear of the timestamp corner, passing contrast and 320px legibility; exported thumbnail.png.
